coverage_notes: Exhaustive sweep across node-graph libraries and editors (AntV G6, Rete.js, Reaflow, Baklavajs, Neovis.js, Popoto.js, NetworkX) with strategic expansion to competitive alternatives (React Flow, Cytoscape.js, D3.js, Sigma.js, mxGraph, JointJS, jsPlumb, litegraph.js, GoJS, ECharts, Blockly) and foundational HCI/visualization theory. Sourcing strategy: (1) Official product pages & docs (T0/T1), (2) Third-party review aggregators and comparisons (T2), (3) HN/Reddit/developer blog discussions and academic HCI foundations (T3/T2), (4) Performance benchmarks and market surveys. Deduplication applied across npm trends sites and multiple versions of the same content. Notable gaps: Specific funding/VC investment data for node editor libraries (most are open-source without disclosed funding); G2/Capterra reviews are sparse for technical libraries vs consumer software; detailed UX teardowns of specific libraries. Coverage reflects the practical reality that node editors are primarily technical/developer tools rather than SaaS products with traditional review profiles.
